correctness.rationale: The Prüfer bijection and character product expansion yield an exact inclusion-exclusion sum for every n>=2 and every Walsh character. At even n>=4 the j=1 term is a 2-adic unit times 2k; the binomial valuation inequality and the even-factor bound place every remaining term one power deeper, including the j=0 term. The n=2 empty-code boundary and odd n parity are handled explicitly. This proves every eigenvalue nonzero and the complete stated valuation distribution. The gcd follows using weight-zero and weight-one coefficients; parity of the integer determinant gives the 2-adic invertibility assertion. The included standard-library verifier passed 18,541 exact tests using three constructions, with finite checks explicitly not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Cayley-tree leaf sets are a natural, dependent, multiplicity-weighted vertex statistic with forbidden binary profiles, so complete nonvanishing of the Walsh transform is not automatic. The exact valuation of every character for every tree order gives a quantitative arithmetic spectral stratification: all 2^n modes are retained in characteristic zero, exactly 2^{n-1} have valuation one at each even n>=4, and all odd-order convolution matrices are invertible over Z_2. These properties are intrinsic to deconvolution and modular recovery of leaf-profile distributions. The theorem has an infinite all-order scope and is not a finite table or a minor numerical improvement. No unproved Smith-invariant or sharp real spectral-gap consequence is asserted.
